findings.title: Working-hours check rejects split schedules and allows days off
findings.body: The new check returns unavailable when Array.find locates ANY same-weekday working-hour range that the slot start is outside. A host with split hours on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) will have a valid 10:00 slot rejected because it is outside the second range. Conversely, if the host has no working-hour entry for that weekday, find returns undefined, execution falls through to the busy check, and the host can be considered available on a day off. Additionally lines 141-142 set both start and end from the slot start, so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after them is never rejected. The predicate must instead require that at least one range fully contains [slotStart, slotEnd].

findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot is deemed inside a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every check at the end of the function. Therefore a fixed or round-robin host who has a date override covering a time but also has a Cal booking or connected-calendar event at that time is reported available, and the slot remains bookable (for round-robin the host also remains in slot.userIds). Date-override availability must still be intersected with busy times.

findings.title: Date-override matching mishandles multiple ranges and boundary-straddling slots
findings.body: The find callback returns true as soon as the slot is outside the first override for that date, so a slot contained in a second override range on the same date is rejected. The containment test is also incomplete: a slot that starts before an override starts but ends inside it triggers neither the slotEnd<=overrideStart nor slotStart>overrideEnd branch, so it is treated as inside although part of the event lies outside the override; a slot starting exactly at override end is likewise treated as inside because isAfter is false. Slots should be accepted only when some override satisfies slotStart >= overrideStart and slotEnd <= overrideEnd.

findings.title: Empty date-override comparison is always false
findings.body: Line 114 compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which compares object identity and is always false, so the special case for a zero-length override (start equal to end, used to mark a date unavailable) is dead code. A slot straddling that instant (slotStart before it and slotEnd after it) then falls through, dateOverrideExist is true, and the function returns the host as available on a day they marked unavailable. The instants must be compared with isSame/valueOf.

findings.title: Timezone-converted override loses day rollover across midnight
findings.body: The converted override start/end are reduced to hour()*60+minute(), discarding any day shift produced by adding the invitee-organizer offset. If applying the invitee offset pushes the override end past local midnight, endTime wraps to a small value while startTime stays large, so buildSlots discards the range as start>=end and the override disappears entirely (both the pre-midnight part on the start day and the post-midnight part on the next day, which activeOverrides will not select because the override did not start that day). Minutes outside the 0-1439 range, or an explicit split at midnight, are needed.

findings.title: No test exercises the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The only added test is a second timezone query on the pre-existing single-user scenario (hosts: [], no ROUND_ROBIN schedulingType). The PR's primary claim - that a fixed host's date override restricts a round-robin event while round-robin hosts remain bookable - and the new checkIfIsAvailable path for fixed/loose hosts are therefore never exercised, so regressions such as split working hours, multiple override ranges, or overrides combined with busy bookings would pass this suite.
